channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: European countries in talks with Tehran for Hormuz transit, Iran state TV says
item.description: European countries began talks with Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy for transit through "Following the passage of ships from East Asian countries, notably China, Japan and Pakistan, we received information today indicating that Europeans have also begun negotiations with the Revolutionary Guards navy" to get permission to pass, state television reported.

item.title: "Felt Like Being In India": PM Modi praises Indians In Netherlands
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the Netherlands and praised the Indian diaspora. PM Modi in Netherlands LIVE Updates: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is on a five-nation tour from May 15 to 20, during which he visited the United Arab Emirates as part of the first leg of the visit.

item.title: Donald Trump does ‘not feel optimistic’ for Jimmy Lai after speaking with Xi Jinping
item.description: United States President Donald Trump spoke with Chinese leader Xi Jinping about jailed Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai. Trump raised Lai's case during their talks. Xi Jinping described the situation as "a tough one." Lai's family had hoped for his release.

item.title: Colorado governor commuted Tina Peters’ sentence after Trump blocked funding for clean water
item.description: Steve Cohen will not seek re-election to the U. S. House of Representatives. Tennessee's Republican-controlled legislature redrew his Memphis-based district. Cohen stated the new map was designed to defeat him. He has represented the ninth congressional district since 2007.

item.title: Trump’s lack of focus on human rights in China is big departure for US diplomacy
item.description: Donald Trump did not raise the case of jailed activist Jimmy Lai with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Trump stated he would bring up Lai's case before his departure. He then compared it to asking if he would let former FBI Director James Comey out of jail.

item.title: Where is Dela Rosa? Philippine senator outmanoeuvres president in evading arrest
item.description: Senator Ronald dela Rosa evaded arrest at the Philippine Senate building. Chaotic week in which enforcer of ‘war on drugs’ flees senate building leaves government looking ‘incompetent’The wanted man outran security agents, rallied protesters and even serenaded the media with a military hymn. Then, after a sudden exchange of gunfire, the Philippines’ most controversial lawmaker slipped out of the heavily guarded senate building in the middle of the night.

item.title: CIA director's visit to Cuba echoes past memories of U.S. in Latin America
item.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a surprise visit to Cuba. CIA Director John Ratcliffe makes a surprise visit to Cuba as the spy agency calls on the nation to make "fundamental changes." Cuba says it has run out of fuel and is suffering massive blackouts.

item.title: Dozens of European countries sign up to special tribunal plan to prosecute Russia
item.description: More than 30 countries agreed to join a future special tribunal for At talks in Moldova, more than 30 countries have said they will join a future special tribunal for Ukraine prosecuting Russia over its invasion. How the body will force Russians to stand trial is not clear.

item.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
item.description: Mali's armed forces, aided by Russian mercenaries, conducted airstrikes against a coalition of Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists. This offensive follows an advance by the rebel alliance. The junta is working to retain control amid the ongoing conflict in the west African nation.

item.title: As war displaces millions in DR Congo, new schools offer children hope beyond violence
item.description: New schools are opening in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ten-year-old Shadrac Anyazaka does not hesitate when asked about his future. “After finishing my studies, I would like to become President of the Republic one day,” he tells visitors to his school in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

item.title: Somalia at ‘real risk of famine’ as Middle East war fallout continues
item.description: UN aid teams warned Somalia faces a real risk of famine. At least six million people in Somalia are going days without enough food, UN aid teams warned on Friday, highlighting that nearly two million of this number are young children “at high risk of illness or death”.

item.title: Furnace Creek sizzles as snow sweeps Siberia in a week of extremes
item.description: Honduras recorded its all-time May maximum temperature twice this month. item.title: CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims
item.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Cuban officials in Havana. The Cuban government stated the meeting aimed to improve dialogue. This occurred amid complex bilateral relations between the two countries. CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims.

item.title: HIV prevention and treatment services faltering, warns UNAIDS
item.description: UNAIDS warned that HIV prevention and treatment services are faltering. Decades of gains in the fight against AIDS are under growing threat as donor funding declines and community-based health services collapse in some of the world’s most vulnerable countries, the head of the joint UN programme on HIV/AIDS warned on Thursday.

item.title: Malnutrition in Somalia, hunger crisis in DR Congo, energy shortages in Cuba
item.description: UN-backed food security experts warned nearly six million people in Nearly six million people in Somalia – almost a third of the population analysed – are projected to face acute hunger between April and June, with 1.9 million expected to experience emergency levels, UN-backed food security experts warned on Thursday.

item.title: UN welcomes $1.8 billion US boost for humanitarian operations
item.description: The United States announced $1.8 billion in new humanitarian funding. This boost will support United Nations and partner aid operations globally. The funding arrives as rising needs and shortfalls force agencies to reduce assistance. An additional $1.8 billion in US humanitarian funding will allow the United Nations and its partners to expand emergency relief operations reaching millions of people worldwide, as rising global needs and funding shortfalls force aid agencies to scale back assistance.

item.title: Yemen parties agree under UN mediation to release 1,600 detainees
item.description: Yemen's warring parties agreed to release over 1,600 detainees. The deal was brokered by the United Nations in Jordan. This marks the largest prisoner exchange since the civil war began. The agreement offers a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts. More than 1,600 conflict-related detainees in Yemen will be released under a UN-brokered agreement reached after months of negotiations in Jordan, marking the largest prisoner release deal since the country’s civil war began and offering a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts.
